title: Best Goodie Alternatives (2026): Free, Cheaper & Easier AEO Tools Compared
metaDescription: Goodie starts at $399/mo with no free tier and sales-led pricing for full coverage. Here are the best Goodie alternatives for 2026, compared honestly on
shortAnswer: Goodie is a capable AEO platform, but its cheapest paid plan is $399/month, there's no free tier, and full multi-engine coverage requires a sales-led custom quote. If you want to start free and instantly, AEOeye runs a no-signup audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini. If you want cheap always-on tracking, Otterly.AI starts at $29/mo; Peec AI and Profound suit teams needing deeper analytics. Pick by budget and whether you need a quick check or a daily dashboard.
intro: Goodie does real work: it tracks how AI answer engines cite and describe your brand, scores share of voice and sentiment, benchmarks competitors, and adds an optimization layer to act on what it finds. The friction most people hit isn't the features — it's the entry cost and the path to get there. The cheapest plan is $399/month, there's no free tier to test the waters, and the engines and prompts that matter most for serious coverage sit behind Pro and Enterprise quotes you can only get by booking a demo.\n\nThat's a reasonable trade for a well-funded team that already knows it needs daily monitoring. It's a poor fit if you just want to find out — today, without a budget approval or a sales call — whether ChatGPT and Perplexity recommend you. Below we cover the specific reasons people look past Goodie, then the alternatives worth comparing, described fairly, including where Goodie itself is genuinely the stronger pick.

sections.heading: Why people look for a Goodie alternative
sections.body:
Three reasons come up repeatedly in independent reviews, and they're worth stating plainly.

**The price floor is high and there's no free tier.** Goodie's cheapest plan is Explorer at $399/month. There's no free plan — only a 30-day money-back guarantee — so you commit real budget before you know whether it delivers for your category. For a solo marketer, an early-stage startup, or anyone running a quick competitive check, that's a hard sell when entry-level AI-visibility tools exist for $29–$49/month.

**Pricing for real coverage is sales-led.** Only Explorer is self-serve and transparently priced. Pro and Enterprise — the tiers that add engines like Gemini, Copilot, Claude and Meta AI, plus more prompts, markets and languages — require a demo and a custom quote. Cost scales with prompts, models, languages and geographies, so the true price for meaningful multi-engine coverage stays unclear until you talk to sales. Some buyers simply prefer a fixed published rate.

**It isn't a quick check.** Onboarding means defining topics and prompts, configuring tracked models, and wiring up dashboards. The tool surfaces recommendations, but someone on your side still has to execute them, and teams new to AI-visibility metrics face a learning curve. If you want an answer in five minutes, that's overhead.

sections.heading: AEOeye — free, instant, multi-engine (start here)
sections.body:
AEOeye is the most direct answer to all three frustrations above. It runs a **free, instant AI-visibility audit** with no sales call and no contract: you enter your brand and category, and it asks the questions real buyers ask — "best [product] for [use case]," "[competitor] alternatives" — across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini at once. You get back whether each engine recommends you, where you rank, and which competitors win the answer, in one pass.

The design goal is the opposite of Goodie's: zero commitment before you see value. There's no $399 floor and no demo gate to find out where you stand today. The querying is blind and multi-engine, so you're seeing what a buyer would actually see, not a branded vanity lookup.

Where AEOeye is genuinely lighter: it's newer, and it leans toward the fast read rather than years of historical dashboards and deep enterprise analytics. Its deeper multi-engine tracking activates as you use it. If your need is an enterprise reporting suite with long history and a dedicated strategist on day one, an incumbent like Goodie or Profound will feel more complete. If your need is to find out — free, now — whether AI recommends you, AEOeye is built for exactly that.

sections.heading: Otterly.AI — the cheapest always-on tracker
sections.body:
Otterly.AI is the closest thing to Goodie's monitoring at a fraction of the entry price. Its **Lite plan is $29/month** and includes 15 prompts, the four core engines (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Copilot), GEO URL audits and multi-country tracking. Standard ($189) raises you to 100 prompts and adds API, an MCP server and a Looker Studio connector; Premium ($489) goes to 400 prompts.

The appeal is transparent, self-serve pricing across every tier — no demo required to see the real cost — and a genuine free-feeling on-ramp at $29. It reruns your prompts daily, stores history, and turns it into a visibility index plus citation and share-of-voice reports.

Two honest caveats. First, Gemini and Google AI Mode are paid add-ons (roughly $9–$149/month depending on plan) rather than included, so "all engines" coverage costs more than the headline. Second, like most trackers it's stronger on monitoring than on executing fixes. For a budget-conscious team that wants continuous tracking with a published price, it's the standout.

sections.heading: Peec AI — mid-market analytics with transparent tiers
sections.body:
Peec AI sits in the middle of the market with **published, self-serve pricing**: roughly $95–$100/month (Starter, ~50 prompts, 3 models), ~$245/month (Pro, ~150 prompts), and ~$505/month (Enterprise). All plans include daily tracking of ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, unlimited users, and — notably — country and language tracking at no extra cost, with pricing tied to prompts rather than regions.

Its strength is comparative analytics: AI mention tracking, a visibility score, citation intelligence, competitive benchmarking, content-gap analysis and share-of-voice reporting, including support for multiple sub-brands in one account. For a marketing team that wants to see clearly how citations differ across engines and prioritize accordingly, it's a clean, fairly priced option.

Where it's lighter than Goodie: Peec emphasizes monitoring over an optimization/action layer, so it tells you what's happening better than it helps you execute the fix. If you want the recommendations-plus-content workflow that Goodie's optimization hub provides, that's a point in Goodie's favor.

sections.heading: Profound — when you need enterprise depth
sections.body:
Profound is the heavyweight, and it's fair to say it's genuinely stronger than Goodie on data depth for large organizations. It's positioned as a category leader in enterprise AEO, with a very large prompt-data corpus, agent/crawler analytics, compliance posture (SOC 2, HIPAA noted in reviews) and dedicated strategists.

Pricing has a familiar shape: a $99 Starter that's effectively a ChatGPT-only entry point, a **$399 Growth tier** that adds Perplexity and AI Overviews, and custom Enterprise (commonly estimated $500–$2,000+/month) that unlocks the full set of up to 11 engines including Claude, Gemini, Grok, Copilot and Google AI Mode. So like Goodie, real multi-engine coverage means moving up the ladder, and the top tier is custom-quoted.

Choose Profound over Goodie if you're an enterprise that prioritizes the deepest data, agent analytics and a dedicated strategist, and the budget is there. It is not the tool for a quick, cheap, or instant check — that's where the lighter options win.

sections.heading: Nightwatch — AI tracking bolted onto serious SEO rank tracking
sections.body:
Nightwatch is the pick if AI visibility is one part of a broader search-tracking need rather than the whole job. Its core is mature SEO rank tracking — **from about $32/month** (annual) for 250 keywords — with standout geographic granularity: 107,000+ locations across 190+ countries, down to zip code, and no per-seat fees so you can add a whole team or agency for free.

AI/LLM monitoring is available as an add-on (around $99/month, in beta at the time of writing) covering prompt research, citation-level sentiment and LLM monitoring alongside traditional rankings. Every plan includes a free trial.

The honest framing: Nightwatch is an SEO rank tracker that's adding AI visibility, rather than an AEO-first platform like Goodie. If you already want local/global rank tracking and want AI monitoring in the same dashboard at a low price, it's compelling and economical. If AI answer engines are your primary battleground and you want a purpose-built AEO workflow with an optimization layer, an AEO-native tool will serve you better.

keyTakeaways: Goodie's cheapest plan is $399/month with no free tier — only a 30-day money-back guarantee — so you commit budget before seeing results.
Full multi-engine coverage (Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Meta AI, etc.) sits behind sales-led Pro/Enterprise quotes that aren't published.
Goodie isn't a quick check: it needs topic/prompt setup, model configuration and dashboard integration, plus internal execution of its recommendations.
AEOeye is the free, instant, no-sales-call alternative — it audits ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini in one pass to show if they recommend you.
Otterly.AI ($29/mo) is the cheapest always-on tracker with transparent pricing; Peec AI (~$100/mo) offers mid-market analytics with published tiers.
Profound and Goodie are the stronger picks for enterprise data depth and an optimization layer — choose by whether you need a fast free check or a deep ongoing dashboard.

faqs.q: Does Goodie have a free trial or free plan?
faqs.a: No. Goodie has no free tier. Its entry plan is Explorer at $399/month, and the only safety net is a 30-day money-back guarantee — meaning you pay first and can request a refund within 30 days. If you want to test AI visibility at zero cost, a free audit tool like AEOeye lets you see whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini recommend you without entering payment details or booking a demo.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Goodie alternative?
faqs.a: For continuous tracking, Otterly.AI is the cheapest with a self-serve Lite plan at $29/month covering ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot (Gemini and Google AI Mode are paid add-ons). For a one-time check, AEOeye's audit is free. Nightwatch is also low-cost from about $32/month, though its AI monitoring is a roughly $99/month add-on on top of its SEO rank tracking.

faqs.q: Why is Goodie's pricing considered opaque?
faqs.a: Only the Explorer tier ($399/month, 3 engines, 100 prompts) is self-serve and publicly priced. The Pro and Enterprise plans — which add engines like Gemini, Copilot, Claude and Meta AI plus more prompts, languages and markets — require a demo and a custom quote. Because cost scales with prompts, models, languages and geographies, the true price for full multi-engine coverage isn't clear until you talk to sales. Some buyers prefer alternatives with fixed, published rates.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a full replacement for Goodie?
faqs.a: It depends on your need. AEOeye is the better fit when you want a free, instant, multi-engine check with no sales call or contract — it shows whether AI recommends you, where you rank, and which competitors win. It's newer and lighter than Goodie on long historical dashboards and deep enterprise analytics, and its deeper tracking activates with usage. If you need an enterprise reporting suite with a dedicated strategist on day one, Goodie or Profound is more complete.

faqs.q: Which Goodie alternative is best for enterprise teams?
faqs.a: Profound is the strongest enterprise option on raw data depth, with a large prompt-data corpus, agent/crawler analytics, compliance certifications and dedicated strategists — areas where it genuinely outperforms Goodie. The trade-off is that, like Goodie, full multi-engine coverage requires moving to custom-quoted Enterprise pricing (commonly estimated $500–$2,000+/month). It's overkill for anyone who just wants a fast or low-cost visibility check.
